speaker: Doctor
text: Please describe the appearance of the skin lesion you are concerned about, including its size, color, and any changes you've noticed recently. Also, has it been bleeding, itching, or growing?

speaker: Patient
text: 62-year-old male. The patient has recently immigrated to the US from Africa and seeks evaluation for a non-healing, red, crusty lesion on the shaft of his penis and a similar lesion on his left middle finger. Previous treatments in his home country for syphilis and eczema have been unsuccessful. The patient is a smoker, with a history of two packs per day for the last 30 years.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that detailed history; the combination of a non-healing, crusty lesion on the penis and another on the finger in a 62-year-old smoker is concerning for malignancy. Did these lesions appear suddenly or have they been slowly evolving over months? Also, have you noticed any pain, ulceration, or discharge from either site?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Non-healing, crusty, red lesions on the penile shaft and left middle finger. I also have Lesions are painless, History of unsuccessful treatment for syphilis and eczema.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Squamous Cell Carcinoma (Penile and Digital)

REQUEST TEST: Biopsy of penile lesion, Biopsy of digital lesion, HPV DNA testing.
REQUEST IMAGES: Dermoscopy of lesions.
